title: Creating Value
coreMove: A project creates value when its outputs are used, outcomes change, benefits matter, and tradeoffs keep the work tied to strategy after the baseline looks done.

exampleSpecs.audience: project managers checking deliverables after launch
exampleSpecs.stakes: a completed dashboard can hide weak use and weak benefits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people read the same output report differently and get different value results

exampleSpecs.audience: product and project leads balancing local delivery with strategy
exampleSpecs.stakes: funding may keep flowing to tidy work with weak strategic fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer reframes a stuck project lead's delivery view around strategic fit

exampleSpecs.audience: new project coordinators learning value terms
exampleSpecs.stakes: learners may memorize labels without seeing how outputs differ from outcomes and benefits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A learner's confusion becomes the teaching material for the output to benefit chain

exampleSpecs.stakes: a late feature request can distract from the strategic obligation behind approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same review changes after strategic alignment is added to the acceptance check

exampleSpecs.domain: benefits audit of a process change archive
exampleSpecs.audience: PMO analysts reviewing closed project files
exampleSpecs.stakes: closure records may prove outputs while hiding failed outcomes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: An auditor finds the telling detail in existing records rather than a new event

exampleSpecs.domain: software release note before a portfolio check
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tidy release note may hide a strategic tradeoff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A project lead thinks through the tradeoff without external dialogue
